intro: On 10 October 2026, the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam was conducted in three shifts. Shift 1 and Shift 3 have reported summaries, while Shift 2 currently has only partial data. faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level reported for the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 10 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 and Shift 3 were mostly rated as Moderate, while Shift 2 had mixed reports ranging from Easy to Moderate. Because Shift 2 is only partially reported, the overall picture leans toward Moderate based on the fully reported shifts.

faqs.q: How many questions were attempted on average in each shift of the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 10 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 candidates reported attempting between 81 and 87 questions. Shift 3 candidates reported a broader range of 65 to 87 attempts. Shift 2 has partial data with reported attempts ranging from 71 to 94, but a definitive average cannot be given until more evidence is collected.

faqs.q: Which section was reported as the hardest in the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 10 October 2026?
faqs.a: Quantitative Aptitude was most frequently cited as the hardest section in Shift 1 and was also noted as difficult by some respondents in Shift 3. Reasoning was generally easier, and English difficulty varied across sources.

faqs.q: Are the attempt figures for the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 10 October 2026 official?
faqs.a: No. The attempt figures (e.g., 81–87, 65–87, 71–94) are unofficial and derived from candidate reports. SSC typically normalises scores across shifts, so these numbers should be treated as indicative rather than definitive.
